mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 0.5% coincident with a rise in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening consumer demand offset by a construction rebound, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as sector rotation benefits equities.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -0.5% AND HOUST > previous 3-month average
regime_hint: late-cycle consumer softness with construction resilience
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) during triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 0.2 percentage points for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods of two consecutive monthly UNRATE increases above 0.2pp.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals a broad-based contraction in manufacturing activity, which depresses earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods of three consecutive monthly INDPRO declines exceeding -0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and payroll employment (PAYEMS) month-over-month is not possible, but a sharp deceleration in PAYEMS alongside a rise in UNRATE signals labor market stress, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises AND PAYEMS growth < 0.1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during months with rising UNRATE and flat/stagnant PAYEMS growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 1% for two consecutive months, in the absence of a concurrent rise in unemployment, signals weakening consumer demand without labor market distress, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as discretionary sectors underperform.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls > -1% for 2 consecutive months AND UNRATE does not rise
regime_hint: consumer demand contraction without labor market weakness
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods of two consecutive monthly RSAFS declines exceeding -1% with stable unemployment.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate held constant at or below 1% for six consecutive months in a low-inflation environment signals accommodative monetary policy, which supports risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS <= 1% for 6 consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL < 3%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) during periods of six consecutive months with FEDFUNDS at or below 1% and CPIAUCSL below 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.4% for four consecutive months signals a broad-based expansion in manufacturing activity, which boosts earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) during periods of four consecutive monthly INDPRO increases exceeding 0.4%.
